text:
Two issues in the production build based on the Dockerfile 
- after logging in player only sees a starry background, no ship. Pressing W doesn't do anything 
- attempting to warp gives an error: Warp failed: DriftClient: sendWarp requires an open socket

This may be an issue with the websocket setup in docker?
I'll start by exploring the repository and the existing plan.

I've reproduced both bugs and found the real causes. Before I write the plan, five questions.

**What I found (evidence first):**

1. **The Docker/WebSocket theory is wrong.** I booted the built production server exactly as the Dockerfile does (`STATIC_DIR=dist/client node dist-server/index.js`) and drove it with headless Chromium: WS handshake, `auth_ok`, `join_system`, `enter_system`, 10 Hz `entity_update` and the chart REST calls all work. Nothing to fix in the Dockerfile.

2. **Warp error + dead world = one bug in `app/src/client/App.tsx`.** The big client-wiring effect lists `shell` in its deps; `useMenuShell()` returns a memoized object recreated whenever the menu stack changes. Its cleanup calls `client.stop()` (closes socket, clears presence/chat, status `disconnected`), and nothing restarts it because `useFirstLaunch` has a `startedRef` guard. Reproduced on the prod build: pressing `M` flipped status `online → disconnected` instantly; `sendWarp` then throws2 s later. Introduced by TASK-53 (`95504a2`); `npx playwright test tests/e2e/warp.spec.ts` **fails today** for exactly this reason.

3. **"Starry background, no ship, W does nothing" = there is no 3D renderer in the client at all.** `CanvasStage.tsx` is still the TASK-70 raw-WebGL starfield stub. Nothing in `src/` constructs a `THREE.WebGLRenderer` or `Scene`. `ShipMeshBuilder`, `CameraRig`, `ChunkPipeline`, `ClientShipPredictor` exist as unit-tested modules that are never instantiated; nothing maps keys to `client.sendInput()` (only `tests/load/client.ts` does); and `DriftClient` has no `predictor` property, so the ship HUD is empty too (visible in my screenshot: `IN SYSTEM 0`, no speed/hull). This is a missing feature, not a deployment bug.

**Questions** (agree with a default and I'll go):

1. **Scope of this pass?**
   (a) *(recommended)* Both bug fixes **plus** a minimum playable loop: three.js renderer + scene + camera + your ship mesh + `W/S/A/D/Q/E/Space/Shift` flight. Other players, AI ships, star and planets stay invisible for now.
   (b) As (a) **and** remote-entity meshes + seeded star/planet bodies in the same batch (2 extra tasks, ~2 more hours).
   (c) Bugs only — fix the socket teardown, make the missing renderer an explicit on-screen error, no flight.

2. **Ship visibility / camera?** `CameraRig` only supports `"cockpit"` (first-person — you'd still see *no ship*) and `"onfoot"`.
   (a) *(recommended)* Add a third-person chase mode `"external"` as the flight default so the ship is on screen.
   (b) Keep cockpit, and show a ship silhouette/nose in view.
   (c) Cockpit only; "no ship" is then expected, the goal is just that `W` moves you.

3. **Which state drives the ship mesh?** (a) *(recommended)* The predicted client state (`ClientShipPredictor`, already built) with reconciliation from `entity_update`; (b) raw 10 Hz server snapshots with interpolation — smoother-looking but laggy and it's the path TASK-14 exists to avoid.

4. **Production-path e2e gate as a task?** (a) *(recommended)* Yes — a Playwright spec that boots `node dist-server/index.js` with `STATIC_DIR=dist/client` and asserts: claim → `online` → ship mesh on screen → hold `W` → position/speed change → chart open/close → warp lands; plus keep `warp.spec.ts` in the gate. This is what would have caught both bugs. (b) Dev-server e2e only, no prod-path spec.

5. **Anything explicitly out of scope for this batch?** My proposal: on-foot character meshes, terrain/chunk streaming in-world, combat FX, mobile perf work — leave them for later tasks. Tell me if any of those must be in this batch, or if there's something else you want covered (e.g. a Docker image smoke check, even though `docker` isn't available in this sandbox).

Plan written. Only `.ralph/` was touched (plus a running probe server I killed).

**What the investigation found**

- **Docker/WS is fine.** I booted the built artefacts exactly as the image does (`STATIC_DIR=dist/client node dist-server/index.js`) and drove them with headless Chromium: handshake, `auth_ok`, `join_system`, 10 Hz `entity_update` and warp all work. No `app/Dockerfile` change is planned.
- **The warp error is a client bug.** `app/src/client/App.tsx` puts `shell` (a value object re-created on every menu-stack change) in the client-wiring effect's deps, so opening the chart/menu/dock panel re-runs the effect and its cleanup calls `client.stop()`. Reproduced on the prod build: pressing `M` flipped status `online → disconnected` instantly. `tests/e2e/warp.spec.ts` is **red today** for this reason (regression from TASK-53, `95504a2`).
- **The starry background is a missing feature.** Nothing in `src/client` ever constructs a `THREE.WebGLRenderer` or `Scene`; `CanvasStage.tsx` is still the TASK-70 starfield stub, no key path reaches `sendInput`, and `DriftClient` has no `predictor`, so the ship HUD is empty too.

**New tasks (appended after TASK-69; 1–71 untouched and all still `passes: true`)**

| id | what it delivers |
|---|---|
| TASK-72 | Fix the menu-surface socket teardown; extract `useClientWiring`; make `warp.spec.ts` green |
| TASK-73 | Render host: three.js renderer + scene + CameraRig + instrumented rAF loop (starfield ported) |
| TASK-74 | Own ship: predicted state + ship mesh + WASD/QE/Space/Shift flight input + new `"external"` chase camera |
| TASK-75 | Pooled remote-entity meshes (players, AI, wrecks, drones, props) with snapshot interpolation |
| TASK-76 | Seeded star + planets derived from the shared galaxy generators and the `/api/health` seed |
| TASK-77 | Production-path Playwright gate (build → `node dist-server/index.js`, no `.env.local`) + README/ops docs |

`.ralph/prd/PRD.md` gains §13 with the evidence, requirements R-1…R-8, non-goals (on-foot meshes, terrain streaming, combat FX, mobile perf) and acceptance criteria; `.ralph/STEERING.md` now names the red warp spec and points at TASK-72.
